solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Country song about surrounding country

indicators.note: surrounding means the reversed song goes around the other country
about means turning round, so the song word is read backwards

parts.note: an air is a song or tune
Oman is a country on the Arabian peninsula

explanation.surface: A national anthem that celebrates its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses 'country' twice: the first is the definition, the second the Gulf state that the reversed song wraps around.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a nation in south-eastern Europe, bordering Ukraine, Moldova and Bulgaria.

clue.text: More sensitive, overturned Duke's compensation

parts.note: a raw nerve is a sensitive one
D is the abbreviation for Duke, as in peerage lists; the apostrophe-s reads as "has", joining it on

explanation.surface: A touchy duke, toppled from power, claims a payout.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma splits 'More sensitive, overturned' from the duke; it is the sensitivity that gets overturned, not the Duke.
explanation.definitionFit: A reward is something given as compensation for effort or loss.

clue.text: Mother supported by arthritic dog

explanation.surface: An elderly mother leans on her old, arthritic dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arthritic' looks like it describes the dog, but it is its own piece of wordplay; the dog is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful breed of dog.

clue.text: Suggests friendless Billy drinks at home

parts.note: Billy No-Mates is British slang for a person with no friends

explanation.surface: A lonely man called Billy drinks by himself at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy No-Mates is the British nickname for someone without friends, so 'friendless Billy' drops 'Billy' and gives NO MATES.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to suggest them for a post or award.

clue.text: Outbreak in London borough announced locally

indicators.note: locally means in the local Cockney accent, which drops the initial H
announced means spoken, so the borough's name is heard, as H plus a word for spots

parts.note: Hackney is a borough of east London

explanation.surface: An epidemic in an East London district is reported by locals.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys from east London traditionally drop their aitches, so HACKNEY is said as ACKNEY, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acne is an outbreak of spots on the skin, typically in adolescence.

clue.text: After reflection, get a repository to store work

indicators.note: the hidden letters are read in a mirror, back to front
the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the words from the end of "get" into the start of "repository"; read them backwards

explanation.surface: Once you've thought it over, find a place to keep your work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repository' makes a coder think of a repo, and that is exactly where the answer hides, backwards across 'get a repository'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a machine that works is said to operate.

clue.text: Go faster than stalling bikers when half-cut in far-off place

indicators.note: only half of BIKERS is kept

parts.note: to outpace is to go faster than
BIKERS loses its first half, BIK

explanation.surface: Drunken motorcyclists stall and are overtaken on the way to some remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cut' is British slang for drunk, which suits the bikers, but here it simply halves the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the space beyond Earth's atmosphere is as far-off a place as there is.

clue.text: Centre of Great Lake is scary

indicators.note: takes the middle letter of GREAT

parts.note: Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: The middle of one of North America's Great Lakes is a frightening place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Lake' reads as one phrase pointing to ERIE, but 'Great' is only there to give up its central E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and frightening.

clue.text: Wonderful gallery is overhead

definitions.note: overhead is used as a noun, the transparency

parts.note: the Tate is the London art gallery

explanation.surface: Someone praises a gallery with an impressive ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' is a noun here: an acetate is the clear sheet laid on an overhead projector, often itself called an overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: An overhead is a transparency for an overhead projector, made of acetate film.

clue.text: Judge ties up partner

indicators.note: "up" as in "stirred up" or "mixed up": TIES is churned so its letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A magistrate binds up a companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' is a verb, not the person in the wig: to judge a distance is to estimate it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to judge a height by eye is to estimate it.

clue.text: Women's interests unfortunately blocked by male in parliament

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women

indicators.note: blocked by means the shuffled letters have something lodged inside them
unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of interests are the fodder

explanation.surface: Women's causes are sadly obstructed by a man in the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled INTERESTS is blocked by M in its middle; 'in parliament' is a link plus the definition, Westminster being where the UK Parliament sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster, the London district housing the Houses of Parliament, is used as a byword for the UK legislature.

clue.text: Put away jumper having removed two coats

indicators.note: removing two coats strips the word of two outer layers, its first and last letters twice over

parts.note: a jumper is the British word for a sweater

explanation.surface: Someone stows a sweater after taking off two layers.
explanation.walkthrough: Peeling two layers from SWEATER loses S and R, then W and E. 'Put away' is the idiom for eating food.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away food is an informal idiom for consuming it, especially in large amounts.

clue.text: Singer breaks rules

indicators.note: SINGER is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A vocalist flouts the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rules' looks like a plural noun beside 'breaks', but it is a verb: the monarch rules, or reigns.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: a monarch who rules a country reigns over it.

clue.text: Regularly targeted by FA, Roberto Mancini originally managed Forest

indicators.note: takes every other letter of TARGETED
takes the first letters of Roberto and Mancini

parts.note: the initials of the football manager

explanation.surface: A football story: the FA keeps going after Roberto Mancini, who once managed Nottingham Forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Nottingham Forest is an English football club, so 'managed Forest' reads as a job; here Forest is the definition, a stand of planted trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a plantation of trees grown for timber is a managed forest.

clue.text: Discontinuing accomplished mischief-making?

parts.note: a pro is accomplished, a professional

explanation.surface: Someone skilled at causing trouble is asked to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: To prorogue Parliament is to discontinue its session without dissolving it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proroguing a parliament discontinues its sittings.

clue.text: Tense optimist's view?

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'I will have finished'
an optimist expects everything ahead to be perfect

explanation.surface: An anxious optimist looks ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective describing the optimist, but it is the grammar noun: the future perfect is the tense of 'I will have done'.
explanation.definitionFit: The future perfect is a verb tense; an optimist also sees a perfect future.

clue.text: Republican drops in on President for collection of pipes?

indicators.note: drops in means the letter falls lower in the word, in this down clue

parts.note: Recep Tayyip Erdogan is the President of Turkey

explanation.surface: An American politician pays a visit to a head of state about his pipe collection.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a letter that drops moves further down the word. The question mark flags that a reed organ is not literally a collection of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ, such as a harmonium, makes its sound from a set of vibrating reeds rather than pipes.

clue.text: In general, answer was recalled with difficulty

indicators.note: called back, so WAS is read backwards

explanation.surface: Broadly speaking, the answer was hard to remember.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' pretends to mean remembered; here it only sends WAS back the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: As a whole means taken all together, in general.

clue.text: What fraud investigators aim to do for proceedings in court

definitions.text: What fraud investigators aim to do
definitions.meaning: to squash is to crush; rackets are criminal scams
the bats used in the game of squash, played on a court

explanation.surface: Investigators pursue fraudsters through the legal system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court; it is a squash court, and the rackets are what you play with there.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: crushing criminal schemes, and the equipment for a game played on a squash court.

clue.text: Universal acclaim for lift

explanation.surface: Everyone applauds a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, hence universal.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain, rather literary synonym: to raise something up.

clue.text: Weapon is flipping expensive on 5th of November

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so IS is read back to front
takes the fifth letter of November

explanation.surface: Fireworks for Bonfire Night cost a ridiculous amount.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5th of November is Bonfire Night in Britain, and 'flipping' looks like a mild British oath before 'expensive'; both are just instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a weapon worn at the side, such as a pistol.

clue.text: Lean on body part

parts.note: to lean towards something is to tend towards it

explanation.surface: Rest your weight on part of your body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like the adjective for a fit body; it is the verb, to incline or tend.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a part of the body joining muscle to bone.

clue.text: African natives fight unruly Goths

indicators.note: unruly means refusing to stay in line, so the letters of GOTHS break ranks into a new order

explanation.surface: Local tribesmen take on a band of barbarian Goths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'African natives' suggests people, but the natives are animals: warthogs are wild pigs native to Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Warthogs are wild pigs native to Africa.

clue.text: Large animal in river

explanation.surface: A big beast wallowing in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as a link telling you where the animal is, but it is the wordplay: in = HIP. The hippo really does live in rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is a very large African animal.

clue.text: Draw lots, briefly, to follow leader in Denmark

indicators.note: to follow means this piece comes after the Danish letter
the leader of a word is its first letter
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone is told to pick lots to decide who goes after the Danish leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw lots' looks like a single phrase, but Draw is the definition and lots is OODLES, shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: To doodle is to draw idly or absent-mindedly, making scribbles and sketches.

clue.text: Manager is stud

definitions.meaning: the person in charge at work
a raised knob, as on a shield or a vaulted ceiling

explanation.surface: The man in charge is a ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stud' reads as a lothario; it is a raised knob or ornament, which is also a boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a manager, and also a round stud on a shield or ceiling.

clue.text: Charm bird removing clothing

indicators.note: removing the clothing strips the outer letters, leaving only the inside

parts.note: the robin is a common garden bird

explanation.surface: A bird charmer strips off.
explanation.walkthrough: Obi, also spelt obeah, is a form of Caribbean folk magic, and so a charm or fetish.
explanation.definitionFit: Obi is a Caribbean term for a magical fetish or amulet, used in obeah sorcery.

clue.text: Lad snooping around toxic chemical storage facility

indicators.note: LAD SNOOPING is turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A boy pokes about a plant where toxic chemicals are stored.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds industrial, but the 'facility' is in an animal's body: a snake's poison gland stores its venom.
explanation.definitionFit: A poison gland secretes and holds venom in an animal.

clue.text: Soon, entrepreneur on vacation will meet presidential adviser, once head of government

indicators.note: ENTREPRENEUR is emptied, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: Elon Musk, who advised President Trump

indicators.note: takes the first letter of government

explanation.surface: A businessman back from holiday is soon to meet a former head of state's adviser.
explanation.walkthrough: The entrepreneur and the presidential adviser look like the same man, and he is: Elon Musk. But only ELON counts; the entrepreneur gives just its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaism: ere means before, so ere long is before long, meaning soon.

clue.text: He puts people out with article on kinky sex

explanation.surface: A bouncer ejects customers over an article about kinky sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puts people out' sounds like throwing them out or annoying them; the Sandman of folklore puts people out by sending them to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandman is the folk figure who sends people to sleep.
